name: Saudi Arabia

findings.summary: stc signed an agreement with Huawei for a 5G-ready network at GITEX 2017, alongside separate Nokia capacity and Ericsson managed-services deals; Huawei signed a further 5G technology agreement with stc in early 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: framework-type agreements, no value or binding scope disclosed. Neither source states Huawei's share of stc's current RAN or core; pre-2020 and still_current not checked, so the map will halve it. Huawei almost certainly remains a major stc vendor, but that is inference.

findings.summary: stc named Nokia as main partner for its 2018 5G launch, deploying hundreds of 5G base stations in western Saudi Arabia; Nokia had earlier signed a 4.5G-Pro capacity deal with stc in 2017.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia is Finnish, so pole third. Coded uncorroborated: Telecom Review covers only the 2017 4.5G deal, not the 2018 5G deployment, and Mobile World Live was seen only as a search result. No value disclosed; current status not checked.

findings.summary: Huawei and Zain KSA signed a memorandum of understanding to develop '5.5G' (5G-Advanced) capabilities, including MetaAAU, carrier aggregation and LampSite indoor coverage, for individual, enterprise and government customers.
findings.analyst_inference: MoU only. Zain launched commercial 5G-Advanced in Riyadh and Jeddah in July 2026 (Telco Magazine, opened) but that article does not name the network vendor, so the Huawei link to the commercial launch is unconfirmed.

findings.summary: Mobily signed a five-year 'Network 2023' memorandum with Huawei covering an end-to-end network review, the 4.5G-to-5G transition, network cloudification, and IT and data-centre strategy.
findings.analyst_inference: MoU, pre-2020; the plan's horizon (2023) has passed and its outcome was not checked, so still_current null.

findings.summary: During Xi Jinping's December 2022 Riyadh visit, Saudi Arabia signed a memorandum with Huawei on cloud computing and building high-tech complexes in Saudi cities.
findings.analyst_inference: Counterpart on the Saudi side not named precisely in the article. Huawei's Riyadh cloud region (Sept 2023) is already in the global PRC cloud layer; this finding records the government-level MoU only.

findings.summary: Nvidia agreed in May 2025 to sell HUMAIN an initial 18,000 GB300 Blackwell chips, with several hundred thousand more planned, for its Riyadh and Dammam data centres; delivery depended on US export approval.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3: purchase agreed with named counterparty and quantity, no value. Commerce's 19 Nov 2025 authorisation (up to 35,000 GB300 equivalent) is in the global US chip layer; actual delivery and installation not confirmed in this pass.

findings.summary: AMD and HUMAIN announced a US$10bn joint effort to deploy 500 MW of AI compute over five years, using AMD Instinct GPUs, Epyc CPUs and ROCm software, at sites in Saudi Arabia and the US.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: described as a partnership/investment, no binding instrument identified. The US$10bn covers both countries; the Saudi share is unknown.

findings.summary: HUMAIN, AMD and Cisco formed a joint venture to deliver 1 GW of AI infrastructure in Saudi Arabia by 2030, with a 100 MW first phase on AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs and Cisco networking.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: JV formed but not operational; ownership shares undisclosed. DCD says it is unclear whether this is separate from SAU-007. Date inferred from the article's reference to the November 2025 chip-approval report.

findings.summary: HUMAIN broke ground on two data centres in Riyadh and Dammam, about 100 MW each, targeted to go live in Q2 2026 as the first step toward multi-gigawatt national capacity.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator HUMAIN is PIF-owned, so pole domestic. Tier 4 (construction started). Builders and financiers not named. Go-live in 2026 could not be confirmed in two searches.

findings.summary: xAI and HUMAIN announced at the US-Saudi Investment Forum a 500 MW AI data centre in Saudi Arabia, possibly the first of several; location, terms and value were not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: neither source says whether xAI (us) or HUMAIN (domestic) will own-operate; DCD notes xAI had sought to lease rather than build. W.Media names Nvidia as principal chip supplier.

findings.summary: DataVolt plans a US$5bn, 1.5 GW net-zero AI campus at NEOM's Oxagon, expected online in 2028; NEOM itself was paused in 2025 and is reportedly being refocused toward data centres.
findings.analyst_inference: DataVolt treated as Saudi-headquartered (domestic); not verified in this pass. Announcement date only known to be 2025. NEOM rethink rests on an FT report via Mobile Europe; whether it affects the campus is unknown. NEOM pause not coded as a reversal: not an AI-stack decision.

findings.local_actor: HUMAIN; Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA)
findings.summary: HUMAIN launched HUMAIN Chat powered by ALLaM 34B, an Arabic model building on SDAIA-originated work; in August 2026 Microsoft agreed to offer ALLaM on Foundry and integrate it with Microsoft 365 Copilot.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: HUMAIN controls the model; no source names a foreign base model, so base_model null (unknown, not confirmed from-scratch). Training compute not stated. Microsoft distribution puts a domestic model on a US platform; it does not change model control.

findings.summary: Alongside the 500 MW data-centre plan, Elon Musk described a partnership to deploy xAI's Grok models across the whole of Saudi Arabia.
findings.analyst_inference: Grok accessed as an xAI service, so pole us. Tier 1: a stated intent; no contract, scope or adopting agencies named. W.Media (opened) did not confirm the Grok element.

applications.null_reason: one search on Huawei/Hikvision safe-city or surveillance contracts in Saudi Arabia returned only general Huawei MoU coverage and a CSIS safe-city overview that does not name Saudi Arabia

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power evidence surfaced; budget spent on other layers

research_gaps: Current RAN and core vendor shares at stc, Mobily and Zain KSA, and which vendor built Zain's July 2026 commercial 5G-Advanced network.
Did HUMAIN's Riyadh and Dammam sites go live in 2026, and have Nvidia GB300 deliveries under the November 2025 Commerce authorisation actually arrived?
Ownership and location of the xAI-HUMAIN 500 MW site; whether any Grok government deployment contract exists.
Is ALLaM trained from scratch or fine-tuned from an open-weight base (SDAIA lineage), and on what compute?
DataVolt's ownership/jurisdiction and the Oxagon campus status after the NEOM review.
Saudi safe-city or police surveillance procurement (Huawei, Hikvision, Dahua) and any HMN Tech submarine-cable landings.
Any use of PRC models (DeepSeek, Qwen) by Saudi government or Aramco; search returned only China-side DeepSeek/Huawei chip news.
